posts.author: C-C-C-Cashmere
posts.body:
Introduction
It is said that the best way to learn is to learn from your mistakes, but sometimes it is even more helpful to learn from others' failures. I have long been wanting to compile a list of games which feature unencrypted project files, for tutorial use and to learn how skilled game makers make their games. I believe that so long as it is not in attempt to copy/emulate the games dogmatically, and rather for creative inspiration and general know-how, then a list of games where the developers have been generous enough to allow players/developers access to their unencrypted files should be taken full advantage of - it's what the developers would have wanted. So without further ado, a list of games with unencrypted project files, which I will edit as need be.
RPG Maker VX Ace

posts.author: JaiCrimson
posts.body:
Shaz said:
You are assuming that just because a game is complete, the game maker is skilled.
I have no doubt there would be games out there that, although complete, would NOT be good to learn from.
Click to expand...
You're assuming that just because a game is bad that you can't learn from it.
You can honestly learn more from a game riddled with mistakes than a flawless work of art. Learning what not to do is essentially the same as learning what to do. Yet learning from flawless works of art is also a good thing to do. Basically... as long as you have the desire to learn there is no such thing as a game that isn't good to learn from...

posts.author: C-C-C-Cashmere
posts.body:
You can honestly learn more from a game riddled with mistakes than a flawless work of art. Learning what not to do is essentially the same as learning what to do. Yet learning from flawless works of art is also a good thing to do. Basically... as long as you have the desire to learn there is no such thing as a game that isn't good to learn from...
Click to expand...
Well, to be honest, if I wanted to open up and learn from a game that was terribly crap, I'd open up one of my own failed past games. The reason why I'd want to open up an unencrypted game would be "wait how did he do this fantastic thing? What about this awesome effect? Oh." It's the same reason you don't get a teacher who is really bad at what they do to teach you what to do, because often they'll give wrong advice. Learn from someone who's done it before, and well.

posts.author: JaiCrimson
posts.body:
C-C-C-Cashmere said:
Well, to be honest, if I wanted to open up and learn from a game that was terribly crap, I'd open up one of my own failed past games. The reason why I'd want to open up an unencrypted game would be "wait how did he do this fantastic thing? What about this awesome effect? Oh." It's the same reason you don't get a teacher who is really bad at what they do to teach you what to do, because often they'll give wrong advice. Learn from someone who's done it before, and well.
Click to expand...
I would agree with the teacher thing if we were only talking about tutorial type games but we're being more broad than that so I think your metaphor is a little off, but I get what your trying to say and I disagree. Perhaps you're giving yourself the wrong advice if you aren't learning from other people's mistakes?
The thing about opening your own past games is that you've only made so many mistakes. Other people have tried other things, so you can look at what did and didn't work for them out of these things you yourself haven't tried yet - and therefore haven't succeeded/failed at yet.
Across many different fields, be it writing or competitive sports, you will learn that some of the most accomplished of the field will give the same advice time and time again. "Never give up, learn from others mistakes before you make those mistakes yourself, etc, etc, etc."
Quote from Bruce Lee, "A wise man can learn more from a foolish question than a fool can learn from a wise answer." Taken from Tao of Jeet Kune Do, which I own. Search online and I'm sure you can validate it yourself.
Basically what I'm trying to say is that you aren't exactly wrong but you can learn EVEN MORE from other peoples mistakes. So go learn! <3

posts.body:
My entry to the game jam held on the forums back in January is unencrypted. The game is called We Love you Harold, and its a dating sim game made using all RTP assets.
I did use a mix of MV and MZ assets in the game. But the game was made entirely in MZ.
Link:
